owners.run_binding: WorkbenchState serverRun (hydration only) and derived requestRun

state_model.request_run: derived on every snapshot: the displayed run while run.source is server and run.contextGeneration equals the current generation, otherwise null; never stored
state_model.binding: hydration only: the generation current at hydration when the server-recorded repository equals the hydrated repository, otherwise null
state_model.ticket_added_field: requestRun, captured at dispatch for KINDS with requestRun: true (generate, candidates); null for every other kind

/generate_patch.control: run-bound: #context.innerText -> ticket.requestRun.context or the fresh empty form

/generate_candidates.control: run-bound: #context.innerText -> ticket.requestRun.context or the fresh empty form

related_unchanged./local_critique context: run-bound, sent with the candidate and no repository; a candidate exists only alongside the run that produced or hydrated it
related_unchanged./apply_patch session_id: run-bound; the backend already refuses to persist onto a session whose recorded repository differs

policies.repository_change: UX.STATE.1 invalidation unchanged; the displayed run stays visible and becomes ineligible
policies.switch_back: typing the old path back is a new generation; the run stays ineligible until explicitly selected again
policies.explicit_history: selecting a run (history link or reload) hydrates it; eligible only when its recorded repository matches
policies.same_repository: inputs that trim to the same repository keep the binding; continuation unchanged
policies.ineligible_form: control empty: the fresh no-prior-context form a New Session page sends; the backend answers Invalid control JSON before any harness decision or model call
policies.hydrated_value: #context.textContent once, after the page's JSON formatting pass: byte-identical to the entry's default-layout request, JSON-identical when the Context tab was visible

entry_behavior.repository_a_to_b: Generate Patch and Generate Candidates sent repo_path B with run A's CONTROL
entry_behavior.switch_back: A -> B -> A sent run A's CONTROL (no binding existed)
entry_behavior.browser_restored_history: historical run A re-rendered with restored input B sent B with run A's CONTROL
entry_behavior.java_two_file_request: repository B (Greeter.java, Main.java) requests carried run A's a.py CONTROL
entry_behavior.layout: #context.innerText carried newlines only while the Context tab was visible

post_behavior.repository_a_to_b: repo_path B with control empty; the real backend answers Invalid control JSON; zero provider calls
post_behavior.same_repository: request bodies byte-identical to the entry (produced and history runs, both handlers)
post_behavior.switch_back: control empty until the run is explicitly selected again, then run A's CONTROL
post_behavior.browser_restored_history: repo_path B with control empty; run A still displayed
post_behavior.java_two_file_request: repo_path B with control empty for both handlers; Java files unchanged; zero provider calls
post_behavior.in_flight: the dispatched request keeps its captured context; its late response is still context_changed
post_behavior.layout: transported bytes identical whichever result tab is visible

limitations: Without an eligible run, Generate shows the backend's generic 'Invalid control JSON', as on a New Session page.

After Back navigation Chromium restores a typed repository into the input after hydration; WorkbenchState reconciles at the next input event or dispatch, and a render in between writes the owned value back.
Continuing from a run after a repository change takes a new selection of that run (history link or reload); there is no in-page run picker.

On a hydration mismatch (only if a browser restores the input before the page script) the server-rendered candidate still takes the hydrated repository, as in UX.STATE.1; Chromium restores after hydration.

performance.method: Chromium, real page after a produced run; median per-operation microseconds of 9 batches x 200 operations. ticket_and_body serializes the Generate Candidates body the way each state's handler does (entry: #context.innerText read plus begin; post: begin plus ticket.requestRun). A second run measured post 44.5 / entry 291.5 us.
performance.requests: no transition or measurement issues a request; every scenario asserts its captured request body
